blocks.heading: Key Concepts
blocks.html:
• Coronary arteries supply oxygenated blood to the myocardium
  • Left coronary artery → LAD (anterior) + circumflex (lateral)
  • Right coronary artery → inferior wall + SA/AV nodes
  • Myocardium has NO O₂ reserve — continuous supply required
  • Coronary perfusion occurs during DIASTOLE
  • Cardiac output = HR x Stroke Volume

blocks.heading: Normal Values
blocks.html:
• Troponin I: <0.04 ng/mL (undetectable normal)
  • CK-MB: <6% of total CK
  • Normal ECG: regular sinus, ST isoelectric
  • Coronary flow: 4-5% of cardiac output at rest

blocks.heading: What the Nurse Must Know
blocks.html:
• Heart perfuses during diastole — tachycardia reduces perfusion
  • LAD ('Widow Maker') occlusion = highest mortality
  • RCA occlusion = inferior MI — watch for bradycardia/blocks
  • Collateral circulation develops in chronic ischemia

blocks.heading: NORMAL FUNCTION
blocks.html:
• Coronary arteries patent → adequate O₂ to myocardium
  • Aerobic metabolism: 32 ATP per glucose
  • Uniform cardiac contraction each heartbeat
  • Troponin intracellular — NOT in bloodstream

blocks.heading: DYSFUNCTION
blocks.html:
• Plaque rupture → thrombus → coronary occlusion
  • Ischemia → anaerobic metabolism (2 ATP only)
  • Cell membrane breaks → troponin leaks into blood
  • Myocardial cell death → non-contractile scar tissue

blocks.heading: ⚠ Risk Factors (Non-Modifiable)
blocks.html:
• Age >45 (M) / >55 (F)
  • Male gender
  • Family history premature CAD
  • African Caribbean ethnicity

blocks.heading: 💡 Risk Factors (Modifiable)
blocks.html:
• Smoking (most important)
  • Hypertension
  • Hyperlipidemia (LDL >100)
  • Diabetes (2-4x risk)
  • Obesity / sedentary

blocks.heading: 🔥 Complications
blocks.html: Cardiogenic shock • Ventricular dysrhythmias • Heart failure • Papillary muscle rupture • VSD • Free wall rupture
NRG Opposite: Plaque rupture blocks blood flow → ischemia → infarction → pump failure

1. Endothelial injury: HTN, smoking, LDL damage vessel lining

2. LDL infiltration: Oxidized LDL enters subendothelial space

3. Inflammation: Macrophages engulf LDL → foam cells

4. Plaque: Fibrous cap over lipid core develops

5. Plaque rupture: Cap tears → collagen exposed

6. Thrombus: Platelet aggregation occludes artery

blocks.heading: Key Detail
blocks.html: STEMI = complete occlusion → ST elevation. NSTEMI = partial occlusion → ST depression/T wave inversion. Unstable angina = symptoms at rest without biomarker elevation.

blocks.heading: Clinical Result
blocks.html: Cell death begins at 20-30 min of ischemia. Irreversible by 4-6 hours. Reperfusion within 12 hours saves myocardium. Goal: door-to-balloon <90 min, door-to-needle <30 min.
NRG Sequencing: Each step leads to the next — understand the cascade to predict S/S and management

blocks.heading: Early / Mild
blocks.html:
• Chest pressure, squeezing, heaviness
  • Pain radiates to left arm/jaw/back
  • Diaphoresis (cold clammy sweat)
  • Nausea / vomiting
  • Anxiety / sense of doom
  • Often: atypical in women, elderly, diabetics

blocks.heading: Severe
blocks.html:
• Crushing chest pain unrelieved by rest/NTG
  • Severe dyspnea
  • Syncope or near-syncope
  • Hypotension, tachycardia
  • New S3 or S4 gallop
  • Jugular venous distension

blocks.heading: Cardiogenic shock: BP <90, cool clammy skin, altered LOC
blocks.html:
• Cardiogenic shock: BP <90, cool clammy skin, altered LOC
  • Ventricular fibrillation → cardiac arrest
  • Pulseless electrical activity (PEA)
  • Acute pulmonary edema
  • THIS IS A MEDICAL EMERGENCY

blocks.heading: Diagnostic / Assessment Findings
blocks.html:
• Troponin I/T: elevated within 3-6 hours
  • CK-MB: rises at 4-8 hours, peaks 12-24h
  • ECG: ST elevation (STEMI) or depression (NSTEMI)
  • Echocardiogram: wall motion abnormalities
  • Chest X-ray: pulmonary edema, cardiomegaly

blocks.heading: Link Patho to S/S
blocks.html:
Coronary occlusion → Chest pain, diaphoresis

Myocardial ischemia → Nausea, anxiety (vagal stimulation)

Pump failure → Dyspnea, JVD, hypotension

Dysrhythmias → Syncope, palpitations, sudden death

blocks.heading: Cardiovascular
blocks.html:
• BP both arms (compare)
  • Apical pulse, heart sounds (S3/S4)
  • 12-lead ECG within 10 min of arrival
  • Check all peripheral pulses
  • Capillary refill, skin temp/color

blocks.heading: Respiratory
blocks.html:
• Respiratory rate and effort
  • Lung sounds (crackles = fluid)
  • SpO2
  • Work of breathing

blocks.heading: Neurological
blocks.html:
• Level of consciousness
  • Anxiety level
  • Pain: PQRST assessment
  • Signs of cerebral hypoperfusion

blocks.heading: Key Laboratory & Diagnostic Tests
rows: ST elevation/depression, Q waves, T inversion

blocks.heading: Priority Actions
blocks.html: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes. ASA 325 mg chew (if no allergy). NTG SL for pain. Morphine if pain unrelieved. IV access x2. Continuous monitoring. MONA: Morphine, Oxygen, Nitrates, Aspirin.

blocks.heading: 💊 Pharmacology - Nursing Monitoring
rows: Reduce HR, BP, myocardial O₂ demand
Hold if HR <60, SBP <90, acute HF
Bleeding risk — CI if recent surgery/stroke

blocks.heading: Beta-Blocker & Thrombolytic Alert
blocks.html: Hold metoprolol if HR <60, SBP <90, or signs of acute HF. tPA: CI if active bleeding, recent stroke (<3mo), surgery (<14 days). Check BP before each NTG dose.

blocks.heading: Lifestyle & Patient Education
blocks.html:
• Smoking cessation (most effective intervention)
  • Cardiac rehabilitation program
  • Low-fat, low-sodium diet (Mediterranean)
  • Gradual return to activity
  • Medication adherence education
🚨 Report Immediately: Chest pain unrelieved by NTG | New dyspnea | Syncope | Palpitations | BP <90/60 | Bleeding (on anticoagulants)

blocks.heading: Nursing Diagnosis
blocks.html: Decreased cardiac output related to myocardial ischemia/infarction as evidenced by chest pain, ST elevation, elevated troponin, and hypotension

blocks.heading: Goal / Outcome
blocks.html: Patient will be pain-free with stable hemodynamics within 24 hours of treatment. Troponin will trend downward.

blocks.heading: Interventions
blocks.html:
• Administer MONA protocol per orders
  • Continuous cardiac monitoring
  • Monitor vital signs q15min x4, then q1h
  • Assess pain q30min using 0-10 scale
  • Maintain bed rest with HOB 30-45°
  • Check puncture site (if PCI) q1h

blocks.heading: Rationale
blocks.html: MONA reduces myocardial O₂ demand and improves perfusion. Continuous monitoring detects life-threatening dysrhythmias early. Pain assessment evaluates reperfusion success. Bed rest reduces cardiac workload.

blocks.heading: Evaluation
blocks.html: Pain 0/10. BP 118/78. HR 72 regular. No dysrhythmias. Troponin trending down. Patient verbalizes understanding of discharge instructions.
NRG Care Plan Formula: Problem → Goal → Interventions → Rationale → Evaluation

What system is being tested?

Cardiovascular — coronary perfusion and pump function

What is the priority?

Reperfusion ASAP — ECG in 10 min, MONA, revascularization

What is unsafe?

Giving beta-blockers in acute HF, delaying ECG, missing atypical presentations in women

What restores function?

Reperfusion (PCI/thrombolysis) restores coronary blood flow

blocks.heading: 💡 Key Memory Aids for RENR
blocks.html:
• MONA: Morphine, Oxygen, Nitrates, Aspirin — but not everyone gets oxygen
  • Troponin timing: Rises 3-6h, peaks 12-24h — single negative troponin does NOT rule out MI
  • Door-to-balloon: <90 minutes for PCI; door-to-needle <30 min for thrombolytics
  • Women/Diabetics/Elderly: Atypical presentations common — fatigue, SOB, indigestion, weakness
  • Beta-blockers post-MI: Reduce mortality by 25-40% — start within 24h if hemodynamically stable
NRG System Focus Formula: ACS → Cardiovascular → Coronary occlusion → Myocardial ischemia → Priority: Reperfusion + MONA + Monitoring

question.stem: A 62-year-old patient presents with crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm, diaphoresis, and nausea. Vital signs: BP 88/56, HR 112, RR 24. The 12-lead ECG shows ST elevation in leads V1-V4. Which nursing action is the highest priority?

options.html: Administer sublingual nitroglycerin every 5 minutes for pain relief
Prepare the patient for immediate percutaneous coronary intervention
Obtain a complete set of vital signs including temperature
Start a heparin infusion after confirming the troponin level

question.rationale: ST elevation in V1-V4 indicates an acute anterior wall STEMI (LAD territory). The patient is hemodynamically unstable (BP 88/56, tachycardic). The highest priority is immediate reperfusion via PCI. Every minute of delay increases mortality. Nitroglycerin is contraindicated with SBP <90. Troponin confirmation is NOT required before treatment — ECG changes are diagnostic.

why.html: NTG is contraindicated with SBP <90 mmHg — could worsen hypotension
Complete vitals are important but do not delay reperfusion
Troponin confirmation is NOT required — ECG is diagnostic; heparin alone does not reperfuse
